artifacts.summary: Phase 1 re-verification of Verified Findings V1-V9 in a disposable scratch repo, plus the authoritative 11-site commit-site inventory across 7 files (a minor correction to the plan's stated 8-file expectation).

Full implementation summary including the three-arm concurrency comparison (baseline reproduces misattribution; path-scoping-only trades it for a 10/30 index.lock failure rate; the full fix achieves 0/0 on both), the 8-concurrent-committer scale run, and both safety-gate assertions under load.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed git index contention between concurrently dispatched agents by path-scoping every git commit in the dispatch pipeline and serializing the git add + git commit pair through a new specs/.commit-lock/ mutex (task-lock.sh's commit-acquire/commit-release verbs), both consolidated into one shipped helper (git-commit-scoped.sh) invoked by all 11 commit sites across 7 files. Empirically demonstrated under real concurrency: baseline reproduces the reported misattribution, path-scoping-only trades it for a 10/30 (~33%) index.lock failure rate, and the full fix achieves 0/30 misattribution and 0/30 failures, plus a clean 8-concurrent-committer run in 0.48s.

memory_candidates.content: A concurrency defect can have TWO layers that must both be fixed together: (1) commit-level path scoping (git commit -- <paths>) prevents cross-process misattribution but (2) alone converts it into an index.lock race under true concurrency (measured ~33% failure rate at 2 concurrent committers in this codebase). The fix is path-scoping PLUS mutex-serializing the add+commit pair -- neither alone is sufficient, and empirical A/B/C testing (bare vs scoped-only vs scoped+mutex) is what proves it rather than reasoning about it. Two more non-obvious git pathspec footguns worth remembering: an exclude-only pathspec list (no positive entry) commits EVERYTHING except the excluded paths -- wider than a bare commit, not narrower; and a single unmatched path in a commit's pathspec list aborts the ENTIRE commit (unlike git add's more forgiving partial-failure behavior in some cases), so a scoped-commit helper must validate and drop unmatched paths rather than pass them through.

When adding a second mutex sibling to an existing named-mutex pattern (e.g. a new specs/.commit-lock/ alongside an existing specs/.scope-lock/), the reentrancy-flag collision is the decisive design constraint, not call-frequency: a single global env flag like SCOPE_MUTEX_HELD=1 means 'an outer holder already owns THIS mutex', so reusing the same mutex directory for a second, unrelated critical section would make an inherited flag either silently skip serialization it should apply, or force a nested acquire on a documented non-reentrant primitive. Two independent critical sections always need two independent held-flags, which in turn requires two mutex directories -- refactor the underlying acquire/release logic into a name-parameterized primitive (e.g. acquire_named_mutex(dirname, ...)) so both mutexes share one implementation without duplicating the mkdir/staleness/wait-budget logic.
